meta.how_to_use: Statements are paraphrased summaries of the linked pages, not quotes. Quote numbers from here, never from memory. Before a submission or when review_due has passed, run scripts/docs/check-docs-freshness.mjs; for every changed page re-read the live page and update the affected entries, bump register_version and researched_on, and log it in CHANGELOG.md.

stage_meaning.basic: Required for Basic Launch (soft launch, 7-21 days, monetization disabled).

type_meaning.mandatory: Stated as a requirement. Failing it can get the game rejected.
type_meaning.guideline: Marked Guideline or best practice by CrazyGames. Strongly recommended, not a hard gate.
type_meaning.guidance: From the Resources section (monetization/launch guides). Advice backed by their data, not a rule.

verification_meaning.auto: A tool in the template decides PASS/FAIL from artifacts.
verification_meaning.browser: tools/qa/browser-qa.mjs drives the build and records evidence.
verification_meaning.manual: A human, or Claude looking at screenshots/video, must judge it. Record with tools/qa/record.mjs.
verification_meaning.portal: Only the CrazyGames Developer Portal preview or CrazyGames QA can confirm it.

corrections_vs_codex_game_factory_regist: gameplayStop must NOT be sent when the player switches focus or leaves the game area (sdk/game). The old template sent it on tab hide.
Data module: rely fully on it on CrazyGames for guests and logged-in users and avoid relying on local saves (sdk/data). The old SaveService mirrored every write to localStorage.
Legibility sizes are ten named iframe sizes including 821x462 (smaller than the old 907x510 floor) and a 1080x607 tablet size (requirements/gameplay).
New SDK calls not in the old register: reportGameCompletedPercentage, setGameContext/clearGameContext, environment 'disabled', applicationType 'pwa'.
Leaderboards (invite-only) and their encryption/API keys; banner refresh cap of 120 per session per size; bannersDisabledMobileApp.
FAQ rejection reasons include clones/asset flips and content targeted at kids.

requirements.title: Initial download <= 50 MB
requirements.statement: Initial download must be <= 50 MB. With the SDK integrated it is measured from the start of loading until the first gameplayStart event, which must fire when the player is in a playable state (not menus or extra loading).

requirements.title: Total size <= 250 MB (<= 50 MB without SDK)
requirements.statement: Maximum total file size is 250 MB. Without the SDK the total size is used as the initial download and must be <= 50 MB (<= 20 MB for mobile homepage eligibility).

requirements.title: File count <= 1500
requirements.statement: At most 1500 files; high file counts slow loading.

requirements.title: Mobile homepage eligibility: initial download <= 20 MB
requirements.statement: To be eligible for the mobile homepage the initial download cannot exceed 20 MB.

requirements.title: Relative paths only
requirements.statement: Refer to bundle files with relative paths only; absolute paths fail to load.

requirements.title: Externally loaded files: gameplay within 20 s
requirements.statement: For externally hosted or loaded files, QA judges the time to reach gameplay, which must be <= 20 seconds.

requirements.title: Works on Chrome and Edge
requirements.statement: Games are expected to work on Chrome and Edge; games that do not work well on Safari are disabled on Safari.

requirements.title: Smooth on a 4 GB RAM Chromebook
requirements.statement: A significant part of the audience uses Chromebooks; games that do not run smoothly on a 4 GB RAM device are disabled on Chromium OS.

requirements.title: Mouse, keyboard, and touch if mobile is supported
requirements.statement: Support mouse and keyboard, and touch when mobile is supported.

requirements.title: Playable in landscape on desktop
requirements.statement: Playable in landscape on desktop. Portrait games are allowed, especially mobile-friendly ones, with black bars or background images at the sides.

requirements.title: No orientation lock logic
requirements.statement: Supported orientations are set in the submission and enforced by the website; the game does not implement orientation locking.

requirements.title: user-select: none on body
requirements.statement: Add -webkit-/-moz-/-ms-user-select: none and user-select: none to the body to prevent the magnifier and selection menus on tablets.

requirements.title: Safe areas inside the CrazyGames App
requirements.statement: Games open fullscreen in the iOS/Android app; pad important UI into env(safe-area-inset-*) so notches and rounded corners do not cover it (detect via systemInfo.applicationType google_play_store / apple_store).

requirements.title: Sitelock must allow every CrazyGames origin
requirements.statement: If sitelocked, allow all CrazyGames domains including games.crazygames.com, https://app.crazygames.com and capacitor://app.crazygames.com. A scheme-less CSP frame-ancestors entry allows only https ancestors and shows a white screen in the iOS app. See domains.json.

requirements.title: Privacy notice when collecting data beyond SDK events
requirements.statement: If the game collects personal data beyond the SDK events, show new players a Terms/Privacy notice; a simple non-blocking notice is recommended over a blocking pop-up.

requirements.title: Resume audio after iOS interruptions
requirements.statement: iOS interrupts the AudioContext when backgrounded; call resume() inside a user gesture (touchend/click). Listening to visibilitychange alone is not enough.

requirements.title: Use SDK system info for device-specific experiences
requirements.statement: CrazyGames strongly recommends relying on SDK systemInfo (device type, OS, browser, application type) for device-specific behaviour.

requirements.title: New users land in gameplay (max 1 click)
requirements.statement: New users should enter gameplay immediately; if not feasible, at most one click is allowed.

requirements.title: Legible at devicePixelRatio 1 at the named iframe sizes
requirements.statement: Text and images must be legible at devicePixelRatio 1 on responsive 16:9 iframes and mobile screens. Most important sizes: desktop non-fullscreen 907x510, 1216x684, 1077x606, 821x462; desktop fullscreen 1366x768, 1920x1080, 1536x864, 1280x720; mobile 800x450; tablet 1080x607.

requirements.title: Physics consistent across refresh rates
requirements.statement: Physics must behave consistently across monitor refresh rates such as 144 Hz and 165 Hz.

requirements.title: Loads quickly, no errors or crashes
requirements.statement: The game must load quickly and play seamlessly without errors or crashes.

requirements.title: English localization; accurate translations from SDK locale
requirements.statement: English is mandatory. Included translations must be accurate and high quality; choose the language from SDK systemInfo.locale and fall back to English.

requirements.title: Intuitive controls on each device type
requirements.statement: Controls must be intuitive on the different device types, respecting the restricted keys.

requirements.title: Original name, assets and content
requirements.statement: Game names, assets and overall content should be original. The FAQ lists unoriginal content (clones or asset flips) as a rejection reason.

requirements.title: No custom fullscreen button
requirements.statement: CrazyGames provides fullscreen; custom in-game fullscreen buttons are prohibited because they can interfere with monetization.

requirements.title: No cross-promotion (narrow exceptions)
requirements.statement: No cross-promotion of external or internal games/platforms. Allowed when not a main-menu CTA: privacy policy/T&C; community links (Discord, dev site) on the menu if they do not lead to a playable web version; Steam/Epic links for desktop games on the main menu or end of a demo; unpromoted backlinks to CrazyGames home/category; links to games in the same series. App Store links are never allowed in-game (use Developer Portal metadata fields).

requirements.title: PEGI 12, audience 13+, not targeted at kids
requirements.statement: CrazyGames' audience is 13+; games must be PEGI 12 compliant. A separate kids site exists with monetization disabled; the FAQ lists content targeted for kids as a rejection reason.

requirements.title: Avoid browser-reserved keys
requirements.statement: Avoid Escape (closes fullscreen) and Ctrl/Cmd+W (closes the tab; can be disabled while fullscreen).

requirements.title: Key bindings adapt to keyboard layout
requirements.statement: Prefer bindings that adapt to the user's layout; on AZERTY (France) WASD is ZQSD. Read KeyboardEvent.code.

requirements.title: In-gameplay, skippable, visual onboarding
requirements.statement: Land new users in a simple onboarding phase inside gameplay, focus on core functionality, make it skippable, prefer visuals over text, show controls with a key overlay or gesture.

requirements.title: Honest buttons
requirements.statement: Buttons are clearly labeled, not sized to encourage ads or other behaviour, and have no delays meant to confuse.

requirements.title: Fun-experience principles
requirements.statement: Clear goals, easy to learn, quick response to input, balanced pacing, comfortable layout and audio, UI designed per device, no overly repetitive tasks; if solo and friends play both exist they are equally prominent, and if solo is unavailable say so.

requirements.title: Unique, honest identity
requirements.statement: Name and imagery reflect the real game; not easily confused with similar names/iconography; no common identifier or trademark you do not own; change name/imagery only for significant updates; genre should not change after submission; update and maintain the game.

requirements.title: Consistent high-quality visuals and audio
requirements.statement: High, consistent resolution; no compression artifacts; one aesthetic style throughout; consistent audio levels; music that fits.

requirements.title: Pointer lock/confinement for mouse-driven games
requirements.statement: First-person: lock the mouse during gameplay with an unlock shortcut (e.g. Escape, Tab). Top-view games where the character follows mouse gestures: lock and confine the mouse, show a custom pointer or joystick, provide an unlock shortcut, keep on-screen buttons clickable or keyboard-accessible. Click-on-UI games need no confinement.

requirements.title: SDK required for Full Launch (HTML5 v3)
requirements.statement: SDK is optional for Basic Launch and mandatory for Full Launch. HTML5: load https://sdk.crazygames.com/crazygames-sdk-v3.js in the head before game code and await CrazyGames.SDK.init() before any use. The v3 SDK is promise-based.

requirements.title: First gameplayStart marks a real playable state
requirements.statement: When the SDK is integrated (even for Basic Launch) trigger gameplayStart when the player reaches a playable state; it measures initial download size.

requirements.title: gameplayStart/gameplayStop on real breaks, not on focus loss
requirements.statement: Call gameplayStart whenever play starts or resumes (start, resume, revive, next level) and gameplayStop at every break (menu, level end, pause). Do not call gameplayStop when the user switches focus or leaves the game area; CrazyGames handles that.

requirements.title: settings.muteAudio outranks the in-game toggle
requirements.statement: Full Implementation requires muteAudio support (HTML5, Unity, Cocos, Construct). When true, audio must be off even if the in-game toggle says on. Listen with addSettingsChangeListener. Test locally with ?muteAudio=true.

requirements.title: Handle SDK environments
requirements.statement: SDK.environment is 'local' on localhost/127.0.0.1, 'crazygames' on CrazyGames domains and 'disabled' elsewhere, where every call throws. Check the environment and avoid SDK use outside local/crazygames; the game must still run.

requirements.title: loadingStart/loadingStop (optional)
requirements.statement: Optional events that let CrazyGames report in-game loading times and fail rates.

requirements.title: Report completion percentage
requirements.statement: reportGameCompletedPercentage(0-100) signals progression milestones; reporting only 100 is enough, intermediate values are encouraged. Endless games define their own consistent milestone. Re-report on load after content updates. Progress should move forward.

requirements.title: Attach game context to player feedback
requirements.statement: setGameContext({...}) attaches state such as level to player feedback emails/portal; clearGameContext() when no longer relevant.

requirements.title: happytime sparingly
requirements.statement: happytime() makes the site celebrate; use it for special achievements (boss, highscore), not for every level or item.

requirements.title: Only CrazyGames SDK ads
requirements.statement: Only ads requested through the CrazyGames SDK are allowed; no external ads at any stage.

requirements.title: Video ads never interrupt gameplay
requirements.statement: No ads while the user plays; show them at logical points (level transition, map change, after death). No midgame ad on navigational buttons (main menu icon, settings, shop). Ads should not appear before a reasonable amount of gameplay.

requirements.title: Pause and block UI for the whole ad request
requirements.statement: The user cannot progress while an ad is requested or shown; requests take time (auctions). Block the UI until adFinished or adError.

requirements.title: Mute on adStarted, unmute on finish/error
requirements.statement: Mute when the ad actually starts (not on request, since there may be no ad) and unmute when it finishes or errors.

requirements.title: Handle adError and continue
requirements.statement: Unfilled requests arrive as adError; the game must continue. Codes: adsDisabledBasicLaunch, unfilled, adblock, adCooldown (usual midgame interval 3 minutes, counting rewarded and preroll), other.

requirements.title: No custom midgame cooldown needed
requirements.statement: CrazyGames paces midgame ads (at most one every 3 minutes, accounting for game start and rewarded ads). Early requests are ignored with no user impact; request at every opportune moment.

requirements.title: Rewarded offers are clearly optional and marked as video
requirements.statement: It must be immediately clear the reward is optional (no hidden/delayed close) and that a video must be watched (e.g. a video icon).

requirements.title: Decline option looks the same as accept
requirements.statement: The request button cannot be misleading: continuing without the ad uses the same size, font, colour, etc. The request button sits in a consistent, accessible location.

requirements.title: No rewarded button on active gameplay screens
requirements.statement: The request button must not appear during active gameplay (e.g. not during a race).

requirements.title: No ad chaining
requirements.statement: Never require more than one rewarded ad for a single reward.

requirements.title: Not too often, not too aggressive
requirements.statement: Do not offer rewarded ads too often (show a timer or hide the button) and do not promote them aggressively. Rewarded ads should be special opportunities.

requirements.title: A non-ad alternative exists
requirements.statement: Provide an alternative to watching (e.g. buy the reward with earned coins). Levels completable only via rewarded ads are not acceptable.

requirements.title: Reward only on adFinished; make it visible
requirements.statement: Never reward on adError. On adFinished make the reward clear (animation/notification). When no ad is available, encourage trying later.

requirements.title: No out-of-lives offer on every death
requirements.statement: Out-of-lives rewarded offers may not appear each time a life is lost; limit frequency (timer) and keep a non-ad alternative. Resource guides suggest revives at most once per session.

requirements.title: Midgame OR continue-rewarded between two levels, not both
requirements.statement: Between two levels offer either a midgame ad and restart, or a rewarded 'keep playing', never both.

requirements.title: Banner placement rules
requirements.statement: Banners only on useful screens open >= 5 s on average; never during gameplay; never blocking UI at any size including mobile; clearly distinguishable from content; at most 2 per screen. Banners can cost performance and UX.

requirements.title: Banner container and refresh limits
requirements.statement: HTML5 static sizes 728x90, 300x250, 320x50, 468x60, 320x100 in a fully visible container of exactly that size; responsive banners fit the container. >= 30 s between refreshes of a container; up to 120 refreshes per session per size; banners are disabled in the mobile app (bannersDisabledMobileApp) and during Basic Launch. Clear banners after hiding them.

requirements.title: Adblock users can play normally
requirements.statement: Never block or penalize adblock users. Extra features may be blocked with a notice explaining why. No pop-ups (they interfere with fullscreen and CrazyGames notices). Never keep rewarded buttons clickable without effect. Turning adblock off usually needs a refresh, so save progress.

requirements.title: Game runs smoothly with ads disabled (Basic Launch)
requirements.statement: Ads are disabled in Basic Launch. If the ads SDK is integrated, QA checks the game runs smoothly anyway and rejects it otherwise, e.g. freezing between levels or rewarded buttons without effect.

requirements.title: Cloud progress save when progress applies
requirements.statement: Unless progress does not apply, implement a cloud save: preferably the Data module; or link your own backend via the User module; or Automatic Progress Save (not allowed with in-game purchases).

requirements.title: Data module: rely on it fully; 1 MB; debounced
requirements.statement: localStorage-shaped API (getItem/setItem/removeItem/clear). Rely fully on it for guests and logged-in users and avoid local saves. Max 1 MB of JSON per user (dataLimitExcedeed). Writes are debounced ~1 s (up to 30 s). Data preloads during init. Guest data migrates to the account on login; logout reverts to guest data. With the Data module or APS, the site reloads the game on login.

requirements.title: Enable Progress Save in the submission
requirements.statement: Select the Data Module option in the submission flow, otherwise calls fail with dataModuleDisabled.

requirements.title: No APS with in-game purchases
requirements.statement: Automatic Progress Save syncs localStorage (HTML5) or IndexedDB PlayerPrefs (Unity) with no code, but relies on local data and is not allowed for games with in-game purchases.

requirements.title: No external login; guests can play
requirements.statement: Disable external logins (Facebook, Google, email). Guests and CrazyGames users can play as guests by default. In-game logout and external login are not allowed.

requirements.title: Automatic account flow on userId
requirements.statement: New logged-in CrazyGames users are auto-registered and logged in; returning users auto-logged in; link on the immutable userId from a server-verified token, never on username. Re-check the user every launch (shared devices, profile changes).

requirements.title: Login button rules
requirements.statement: A 'Login with CrazyGames' button may be shown to guests (top-right is a good spot) but never as the blocking main CTA; it calls showAuthPrompt; never trigger the prompt automatically. Detect guest logins mid-session with an auth listener.

requirements.title: Tokens verified server-side only
requirements.statement: getUserToken returns a 1-hour JWT (auto-refreshed); verify it on your server with the public key at https://sdk.crazygames.com/publicKey.json. Never decode on the client; __dangerousUserId must not be used for authentication. Check isUserAccountAvailable first (false on embedding domains).

requirements.title: Use CrazyGames username and avatar
requirements.statement: Full Implementation shows the CrazyGames username and profile picture; multiplayer games must display CrazyGames usernames. Usernames are 6-20 chars (letters, digits, period, underscore).

requirements.title: Share room state via updateRoom
requirements.statement: Report the room (roomId unique across regions), isJoinable and inviteParams via updateRoom, and leftRoom when leaving, so Join/Invite works from the CrazyGames UI. Avoid (or make skippable) onboarding for players joining this way. Integrate inviteLink for in-game link copying.

requirements.title: Instant multiplayer
requirements.statement: When isInstantMultiplayer is true, launch straight into multiplayer: the first player goes into a new private room with default settings (a mode/player-count screen is acceptable); 20+ player games may drop into public play; the user must be joinable immediately.

requirements.title: Keep the group together between rounds
requirements.statement: After a match, players continue with the same group without navigating the CrazyGames UI: next match in the same room or everyone to the same new room.

requirements.title: Chat respects disableChat and is moderated
requirements.statement: Disable chat when settings.disableChat is true (test ?disableChat=true); CrazyGames may require removing chat after complaints. Chat moderation is required (at least a profanity filter; AI moderation such as Lasso is an option). User-generated content also requires moderation.

requirements.title: Submit lobby sizes
requirements.statement: Lobby sizes are submitted with the build; changes for existing games go through the CrazyGames team.

requirements.title: Joinable at all times; join listener; friends list
requirements.statement: Preferably allow joining existing rooms at all times (spectate during a round) or explain unavailability; handle addJoinRoomListener to avoid page reloads; listFriends can improve joining/matchmaking.

requirements.title: Leaderboards are invite-only, one per game
requirements.statement: Only invited games; one leaderboard per game; weekly seasons Monday to Monday ending 09:00 UTC with reset; configure guide text (<= 50 chars), metric type (XP/KDA/POINTS/MINUTES), incremental flag, sort, min/max score, client cooldown, and an encryption key (client) and/or API key (server).

requirements.title: Encrypt client-side scores; prefer server submission
requirements.statement: Client: AES-GCM encrypt the score with the portal key and call user.submitScore({encryptedScore, score}); responses always look successful and validation is server-side. Server: POST batches (<= 100) to the leaderboard API with X-API-Key, 1000 requests/60 s. Client submissions can be manipulated; prefer the server path when you have one.

requirements.title: In-game purchases: invite-only via Xsolla
requirements.statement: Invite-only, Full Implementation, Xsolla with the CrazyGames userId; only signed-in users may buy; hide purchase UI when applicationType is google_play_store or apple_store; handle payment statuses via webhooks or inventory; hide Xsolla 'back to the game' links; disable closeByClick/closeByKeyboard. Loot boxes/random paid items face sales restrictions in several countries.

requirements.title: Three cover images
requirements.statement: Landscape 16:9 1920x1080, portrait 2:3 800x1200, square 1:1 800x800, with consistent visuals across the three.

requirements.title: Cover content restrictions
requirements.statement: No borders; no text other than the title (no 'New', 'Play now'); no icons or store logos; no copyrighted visuals without rights; not blurry or pixelated. Guidelines: not just a screenshot, keep it simple, title on the cover in a stylized font.

requirements.title: Preview videos
requirements.statement: 15-20 s (cut at 20), <= 50 MB, both landscape 1080p 16:9 and portrait 1080p 2:3. Avoid black screen/logo transitions, black bars, the default cursor, promo text, app/social icons. No fast-forwarding (CrazyGames speeds up slightly), no sound, static cover as the opening frame. Animated video is allowed if it represents gameplay.

requirements.title: Qualitative metadata
requirements.statement: Submission includes a game description and controls (plus covers and videos).

requirements.title: Test in the Developer Portal preview
requirements.statement: The Developer Portal preview (crazygames.com/preview) runs the game as on CrazyGames, checks requirements and gives SDK feedback. It is the only place Xsolla tokens work.

platform_facts.statement: Basic Launch ends when the game has been live >= 7 days AND has >= 500 plays; without 500 plays it ends after 21 days. Outcomes: invited to Full Launch, invited to improve and request another Basic Launch, or cannot proceed (resubmit only as a new game with significant improvements).

Progression to Full Launch is benchmarked on average playtime, conversion to gameplay and retention. Multiplayer titles needing a large audience, or invited games already published elsewhere, may skip Basic Launch.

Basic Launch KPI tracking is automatic without the SDK; if the SDK is integrated ads stay disabled. The dashboard updates daily; Day 1 retention needs an extra day. Updates can be made any time and are auto-approved during Basic Launch.

QA rejection reasons named in the FAQ: bugs or broken mechanics, missing English, unoriginal content (clones or asset flips), inappropriate themes, not meeting requirements/T&C/ethical standards, not PEGI-12, content targeted for kids. Rejected games may be resubmitted after meaningful improvements.
Updates are usually processed within the same working day; Basic Launch game and art updates go live instantly. Acceptance is communicated by email.
Successful titles often reach 10+ minutes average play time; strong games 10-15% Day 1 retention; top titles convert 80%+ (players playing >= 1 minute), load in under 10 s and are under 20 MB.
Hypercasual: 8.6 min average play time, 6% D1. .io: 9 min, 5.7% D1.

Platform average D1 retention 6.7%. Strategy 17 min / 7.5% D1 / 21 ad impressions per play (14 rewarded); adventure 17 min / 7.4% / 9.8 impressions (4.5 rewarded); simulation 14 min / 7.4% / 7.9 impressions (3.3 rewarded).
Puzzle is the largest category in the top 100 by earnings: 21 min play time, 6.2% D1, 68% conversion, 8.9 impressions per play (4.2 rewarded, 4 midgame).
Action: ~13 min, 8.1% D1. Shooting: 12 min, 6.5% D1.
Clicker: 15 min, 6.6% D1, 5.5 impressions per play (about half rewarded).
Word: 14 min, 7.6% D1, 71% conversion, 7.9 impressions per play (2.8 rewarded, 4.8 midgame).
Driving: 8.7 min, 5.7% D1, 7 impressions per play, often over-relying on forced midgame ads.

Midgame ads often make 40-60% of casual-game earnings. Wait until the tutorial is done or 3-5 minutes / level 3-4 before the first midgame ad. If retention drops after adding ads, move them rather than requesting fewer.

Rewarded ads have the highest eCPM. Scale rewards with progress (e.g. share of next upgrade cost); consider daily caps (e.g. 5/day) and diminishing returns; say what the reward is ('Watch ad for +50 gems') and show a video icon; cap revives at once per session.

Banners: flush against a screen edge, 10-15 px from clickable UI (puzzle guide says 15-20 px), bottom for landscape, top for portrait, side columns on wide desktop menus; revenue only if visible >= 5 s; hide during gameplay.

Hypercasual: request the midgame ad when the player clicks 'Next Level' after a summary screen; revive with a 5 s countdown, once per session, with 2-3 s invincibility; ad-gated skins, mystery boxes, try-before-buy; menu banners.

Payouts are monthly once the balance reaches EUR 100 (rolls over otherwise), via wire transfer or PayPal. Revenue eligibility: SDK integrated, no branding from another portal, no external ads, original and distinguishable from existing games.

Ranking uses engagement metrics (play count, average playtime, retention, conversion, player feedback), personalized by device, country and OS. New games may get an initial boost; a new-games carousel is on the homepage.

CrazyGames hosts only game files (on a CDN, no cache invalidation needed) and provides no multiplayer servers; bring your own (Photon is named as an example). Games hosted on other portals are not iframed.

50M+ monthly players, strongest in the US, UK and other English-speaking/Tier 1 markets; teenagers skew to competitive .io games, older players to puzzle games. 35M+ players have a CrazyGames account (account-integration page).
Technical SDK integration support is offered once a developer's games reach 50k combined plays. ByteBrew (free) is recommended for advanced analytics.

systemInfo: countryCode, locale, device.type (desktop/tablet/mobile), os, browser, applicationType (web, pwa, google_play_store, apple_store). Local testing params: user_account_available, show_auth_prompt_response, link_account_response, user_response, token_response; also useLocalSdk=true to force local mode on other hosts.
